..(Saturday night through Thursday)
Issued at 412 AM EST Fri Nov 13 2026

The long term forecast period features a return to tranquil sensible 
weather conditions across Eastern Kentucky. The longwave troughing 
feature responsible for the active weather in the short term 
forecast period is progged to propagate off to the east on Sunday, 
with an amplified ridge building into the region in its wake. The 
synoptic-scale subsidence downstream of that ridge axis will keep a 
broad surface high pressure system in the vicinity of the forecast 
area for much of the upcoming work week. It will also reinforce the 
dry nature of the antecedent airmass, which, in turn, will suppress 
precipitation chances and keep skies mostly clear. The forecast 
guidance suite does not resolve that ridge axis east of the forecast 
area until the very end of the period. Therefore, next week's 
sensible weather forecast looks seasonably pleasant, with chilly 
morning lows, gradually moderating afternoon highs, and increasing 
diurnal temperature ranges with each passing day.

When the period opens on Saturday night, there is likely to be 
lingering low-level cloud cover across northern and eastern portions 
of the forecast area. These clouds will act as insulation and keep 
overnight lows in the 30s. So, Saturday night won't be the coldest 
night in the forecast period. The clouds should gradually erode as 
the pattern transitions on Sunday and Sunday night, but their 
continued presence will keep highs cooler and lows warmer than what 
is forecast for later on in the forecast period. With relatively 
less solar insolation present and continued NNW low-level flow, 
Sunday's afternoon highs should struggle to rise above the 50 degree 
mark. Sunday night's lows could remain insulated to the 30s in 
places closer to the WV state line where cloud cover clings on for 
one more night, but the clearing trend should reach western locales 
by Monday morning. Temperatures could drop down into the 20s there, 
but colder temperatures are expected later on in the period, when 
the surface high will be positioned closer to the CWA.

The growing influence of the vertically-stacked ridging will favor 
increasingly efficient diurnal heating and cooling processes. Ample 
sunshine should allow high temperatures to moderate back into the 
50s on Monday, then towards the 60s by midweek. This overarching 
warming trend is supported by modeled midlevel height rises across 
the forecast guidance suite. LREF mean 500mb geopotential heights 
steadily climb towards values that rank between the 90th and 95th 
percentile of model climatology by Thursday. The ridge axis will be 
directly overhead by then, and this corresponds with late-period 
highs in the lower 70s. However, the same mostly clear and dry 
conditions that favor this warming trend will also favor ridge-
valley temperature splits at night. Valley locales are accordingly 
expected to experience well-below-freezing temperatures on Monday, 
Tuesday, and Wednesday nights. The area's conventional cold spots 
(sheltered and shaded hollows) could even climb down into the lower 
half of the 20s, marking the coldest temperature readings of the 
season thus far. The bottom end of the forecast MinT envelope in 
this time frame is contingent upon how low afternoon dewpoints mix 
out, but ensemble probabilities for temperatures less than or equal 
to 25 degrees peak in the 40-60 percent chance range on Tuesday 
morning. It will intrinsically become harder for lows to get quite 
this cold as highs move closer to above-normal values later on in 
the period, but near- to just-below freezing lows are still forecast 
through midweek. Warm air advection on the back side of the ridge 
axis could yield above-freezing lows area-wide at the very end of 
the period on Thursday night, but this WAA isn't accompanied by any 
meaningful low-level moisture return. So, aside from some potential 
frost-related window-scraping on the chilliest mornings, very little 
weather-related societal impacts are anticipated across Eastern 
Kentucky next week.
